When reality-show producer Nadia Kelly accompanies Maple Brook’s social elite to a shooting range, two television formats collide in spectacular fashion. One is Married Justice, a glamorous reality series following wealthy Texas women through their complicated personal lives. The other is a murder mystery where several of those women have excellent reasons to avoid police questioning. It’s the kind of crossover that would give a network executive heartburn and a reality-TV producer the best footage of her career. For The Hunting Wives, it’s practically a normal afternoon.

Rebecca Cutter’s eight-episode second season returns to Maple Brook with considerable unfinished business. Sophie O’Neil (Brittany Snow) knows that Margo Banks (Malin Åkerman) murdered teenager Abby Jackson, and Sophie has her own terrible secret involving Margo’s dead brother Kyle. Their affair has wrecked their marriages, and Margo’s husband Jed (Dermot Mulroney) is running for governor of Texas. A motorcycle gang arrives looking for Kyle, creating another problem that cannot be solved with a carefully worded campaign statement.

The first season established itself as an outrageous combination of erotic thriller, Southern soap opera, and small-town murder mystery. Season 2 pushes each element further, occasionally to the point where the machinery starts rattling.

Yet it’s tremendously entertaining television, largely because Cutter understands how to turn one character’s bad decision into another character’s emergency. The expanding cast and escalating body count eventually weaken the storytelling, but recommending the season is easy. Returning viewers should find plenty to celebrate, provided they accept that Maple Brook apparently has a higher murder rate than some war zones.
